additions.title: The Greenhouse Gas Protocol: A Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard (revised edition)
additions.publisher: Greenhouse Gas Protocol (World Resources Institute and World Business Council for Sustainable Development)
additions.locator: Chapter 4, 'Setting operational boundaries', printed page 25 (PDF page 27); chapter 5 on the base year, printed page 35 (PDF page 37)
additions.quote: Companies shall separately account for and report on scopes 1 and 2 at a minimum.
additions.why: The method behind the emissions line of the basic data set. It defines Scope 1 (sources the company owns or controls) and Scope 2 (purchased electricity) and requires a base year so that figures can be compared over time, which is what makes the data set refreshable. The existing list has the separate value-chain (Scope 3) standard under another criterion, not this one. A voluntary standard published by two non-governmental bodies; this is the revised edition dated March 2004, and later guidance from the same bodies was not read in this pass.

additions.title: The Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations 2013, regulation 12: Recording and record-keeping
additions.quote: must be kept for at least three years from the date on which it was made
additions.why: A binding UK rule under which part of the basic data set already exists. The responsible person must keep a record of reportable injuries, diseases and dangerous occurrences for at least three years, which is the raw material for the health and safety disclosure (B9: work-related accidents and fatalities). The legal definition of a reportable incident is not the same as the standard's 'recordable work-related accidents', so the two counts must be reconciled, not assumed equal. Great Britain; the page shows no outstanding changes.

additions.title: The Equality Act 2010 (Gender Pay Gap Information) Regulations 2017, regulation 1: Citation, commencement, interpretation and application
additions.locator: Regulation 1(2), definition of 'relevant employer'; regulation 2(1) for the six figures to be published
additions.quote: an employer who has 250 or more employees on the snapshot date
additions.why: Settles when the pay-gap line of the basic data set applies to a UK firm. The 2026 regulation asks for the gender pay gap only where the undertaking is already required by law to report it; in Great Britain that duty falls on private and voluntary sector employers with 250 or more employees on 5 April. Below that size the line can be left out. legislation.gov.uk carries this instrument only as originally made, so later amendments are not shown on the page; public authorities listed in Schedule 19 to the Equality Act 2010 are outside these regulations (regulation 1(6)).

additions.title: Making environmental claims on goods and services (the Green Claims Code)
additions.locator: Section 2, 'Business-to-business claims'; section 3, principles 'Claims must be truthful and accurate' and 'Claims must be substantiated'
additions.quote: This guidance also applies (to a more limited extent) to businesses marketing to other businesses.
additions.why: The rule that applies once the data set is published as a sales asset, which is what the top level of this criterion describes. Environmental statements made to win business must be truthful, clear and backed by evidence, and misleading advertising to other businesses is prohibited. A figure with no recorded method cannot be substantiated. Published 20 September 2021 and unchanged on the page read; it describes the law as it stood then (the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 and the Business Protection from Misleading Marketing Regulations 2008) and was not checked in this pass against later changes to consumer law.

additions.title: SMEs and Net Zero 2025: UK Net Zero Business Census report
additions.locator: 'Tracking and measuring carbon emissions', page 17; summary table 'SME Net Zero Key Progress Indicators', page 16
additions.quote: The proportion measuring their carbon footprint comfortably exceeds the proportion where this data has been requested by customers (20%)
additions.why: A UK baseline for the emissions line. One in five smaller businesses measures a full or partial carbon footprint: 10% of those with no employees, 22% of micro, 30% of small and 51% of medium-sized businesses (table, page 16). So an assembled data set is still the exception. Based on 1,783 businesses in the 2025 UK Net Zero Business Census; publication date printed as October 2025. A survey report, not peer reviewed; self-reported; carbon only, with nothing on waste, workforce or conduct data.

additions.title: Data Requests in Value Chains: The Effects of Corporate Sustainability Reporting on SMEs in The Netherlands
additions.publisher: Niemann, Morssinkhof, van der Linden and de Vries, Sustainability 17(17), 8029 (MDPI); copy held in the Delft University of Technology repository
additions.locator: Section 3.3, 'Perceived Relevance of ESG Data for SMEs Themselves' (article page 8, PDF page 9), with Figures 4 and 5
additions.quote: More than half of the SMEs in the sample (52%) indicated that they consider this aspect relevant and that they actively collect data on it.
additions.why: Peer-reviewed evidence on which parts of the basic data set small firms already hold. Health and safety data is the best kept (52%), which the authors link to existing safety law; only 21% both regard carbon emissions as relevant and collect the data, although carbon is the item customers ask for most. Tells a board where the gaps are likely to be. Survey of 431 Dutch firms in late 2024, 19% response rate; Dutch law and practice, not UK. Read in the university repository's copy of the final published version.

additions.title: Engaging small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the low carbon agenda
additions.publisher: Conway, Energy, Sustainability and Society 5, article 32 (Springer)
additions.quote: Whilst the majority has taken steps to reduce their carbon impact, most do not monitor or set targets for managing carbon usage.
additions.why: Peer-reviewed UK evidence for the gap between acting and measuring: small firms take practical steps but do not keep the numbers, which is the 'fragments' level of this criterion. Open access on the publisher's site. Limits: 141 respondents in one English county (Derbyshire), a questionnaire, published in 2015; use it for the pattern, not for a current rate. The British Business Bank survey gives the current UK figure.

additions.title: Fostering convergence in SME sustainability reporting (OECD SME and Entrepreneurship Papers)
additions.locator: Table 2.2, printed pages 18 to 19 (PDF pages 19 to 20); executive summary, printed page 6 (PDF page 7); Annex A, Table A A.1
additions.quote: Most common indicators and metrics across SME frameworks
additions.why: International comparator. The OECD compared the EU voluntary standard with other frameworks for small firms and lists the indicators they share: Scope 1 and 2 emissions, energy, water, waste, workforce characteristics, health and safety, and governance items. The overlap with B1 to B11 shows the basic data set is not an EU peculiarity, so a UK firm that assembles it is also equipped for non-EU askers. Approved 20 January 2025; describes the EU standard while still a draft, before Regulation (EU) 2026/1560 changed some datapoints.

rejected.title: Bridging the SME reporting gap: A new model for predicting Scope 1 and 2 emissions
rejected.reason: PubMed Central returned a reCAPTCHA page. Not bypassed; not read; not cited.

rejected.title: Data Requests in Value Chains: The Effects of Corporate Sustainability Reporting on SMEs in The Netherlands (journal copy)
rejected.reason: HTTP 403. Not bypassed. Read and cited from the Delft University of Technology repository instead.

rejected.title: Questions and answers: Recommendation on a voluntary sustainability reporting standard for small and medium-sized undertakings (VSME)
rejected.reason: Read. Dated 30 July 2025 and written about the Recommendation that Regulation (EU) 2026/1560 has since deprived of legal effect; it adds nothing the list does not already have.

rejected.title: ISO 14064-1 (organisation-level greenhouse gas quantification)
rejected.reason: Not opened. A paid standard; the free Greenhouse Gas Protocol standard covers the same ground and is the one the EU text points to.

rejected.title: Where Next for SMEs and Net Zero? (UKERC)
rejected.reason: Landing page fetched only; the report itself was not read, so it is not cited.

brief_check: Nothing read contradicts the brief. Additions it does not have: a UK baseline (20% of smaller businesses measure a full or partial carbon footprint; British Business Bank, pages 16 to 17); the UK threshold that decides whether the pay-gap line applies (250 or more employees); and the point that a data set published as a sales asset falls under the rules on misleading environmental claims. The brief's 'No UK equivalent for small firms was found' still stands.
